open.speaker: ms_suit
lines: Good evening. Or afternoon. I lose track in the field.
You're the Sutton party. Three of you. Mr Penrose said three. He's rarely wrong about numbers.

passives.line: His shoes are dry. It has snowed since noon. He hasn't walked here from anywhere.
The air near him smells like the inside of igloo 7. Cold, and under it, a struck match.
He stands exactly outside arm's reach. He measured it.

static.line: That isn't a man. Say it to his face and watch what he does with his face.

penrose.speaker: ms_suit
lines: Mr Penrose is my employer. He was here in 1967 and he is here now, and he finds that continuity reassuring.
He asked me to say he's read your founder's work. He admired her handwriting.
He admired it enough to write over it.

stop.speaker: ms_suit
lines: (He takes one step back. Exactly one.) Of course. I'll be where you can see me instead.
Mr Penrose prefers it that way too. He dislikes surprises. He had one here, once.
That wasn't a threat. I think that was a confession.

stop_fail.speaker: ms_suit
lines: I'm not following you. I'm ahead of you. It only looks like following from where you're standing.
Mason Gas, after dark. I'll be there before you. I'm always there before you.

stare.speaker: ms_suit
lines: (He does not blink. After a long time he smiles. It's the smile of a man who has read about smiling.)
You're good at this. She was too.
Don't look at his eyes. Look at the snow by his feet. It isn't melting.

hub.speaker: ms_suit
lines: Ask. Mr Penrose would want me to be helpful. Within reason.

options.text: Your shoes are dry. Where's your car?
Penrose got here first. He didn't get here last. Tell him that.
Room 410. He checked out the morning after the bridge.

car.speaker: ms_suit
lines: At the chapel on Route 62. It doesn't need to be where I am. It's a comfortable car.
You've seen it, I expect. Hollis Pyles keeps very good times. We've read his logbook. He doesn't know that.
Then they've read everything on this road.

car_fail.speaker: ms_suit
lines: I walked. It's good weather for walking, if you're dressed for it.
(It is not good weather for walking.)

first.speaker: ms_suit
lines: I'll tell him. He'll want to know who said it. I'll tell him that too.
She said something like it. On the hotel stairs, the last night. He has it written down.

first_fail.speaker: ms_suit
lines: I'll tell him you were polite. It's kinder. Goodnight, or good afternoon.
(He walks away without turning around first. You don't see how.)

passives.line: You didn't flinch. You'd like that to count for something. It doesn't, not with him.

room410.speaker: ms_suit
lines: Room 410. Yes. Next to hers. He heard her through the wall the last night. Reading aloud, to someone.
He checked out at six the next morning. He crossed the river. He doesn't say how, and I don't ask.
There was no bridge at six that morning.

blink.speaker: ms_suit
lines: Not that I've seen. I've worked for him eleven years.
I was told he blinked once, in 1967, on the bridge approach. Nobody who told me is still employed.
That's a joke. I think that was a joke.
